overview: White declines to take the e6 pawn and plays 5.Bg5, pinning the f6 knight. The common replies are 5...exd5, 5...h6 and 5...Qa5+. In the exd5 line (6.cxd5 h6 7.Bxf6 Qxf6 8.e4) White has a space and centre edge and Black plays for the pawn majority on the queenside and the b-file with ...d6, ...g6 and ...Bb7.

white_ideas.idea: Pin and trade the f6 knight with Bg5 and Bxf6
Keep the d5 pawn and build the centre with e4
Open the queenside lines for the rooks

black_ideas.idea: Recapture on d5 and play ...h6 to question the bishop
Use the queenside pawns and the b-file for counterplay

typical_structures.structure: White d5 and e4 centre against Black queenside pawn majority
Blumenfeld structure with Black pawns on b5 and c5

character.notes: Black plays for activity against a space advantage; tactics around the b5 and c5 pawns.

gambit.notes: In the most played 5...exd5 6.cxd5 line material is level, though other branches (5...h6 6.Bxf6 Qxf6 7.dxe6) do give a pawn.

structure.notes: White pawn on d5 and e4 against Black c5 and b5 with the e-file open: semi-open character.

approach.notes: A respectable but uncommon gambit line used by strong players on occasion.

level.notes: Move orders matter and the structure takes understanding.

sublines_that_differ.name: Blumenfeld: 5.Bg5 h6
sublines_that_differ.how: After 6.Bxf6 Qxf6 7.dxe6 fxe6 8.cxb5 Black is a pawn down in the classical gambit style.

character.reason: Black plays against the centre with tactics on the b5 and c5 pawns and both sides take risks.

gambit.reason: The most played 5...exd5 6.cxd5 line leaves material level, so no pawn is offered.

soundness.reason: Both sides can play it without being refuted.

structure.reason: White gets a pawn on d5 and e4 while Black presses on the queenside and e-file.

approach.reason: A known but uncommon line that strong players use now and then.

level.reason: Needs some theory for the replies, and the plans are not hard.

plans.reason: Black pushes queenside pawns and White builds the centre.
